question: In the epidemiological triad, which component encompasses factors such as age, sex, nutritional status, immune response, and genetic susceptibility?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The host encompasses all intrinsic factors of the individual — age, sex, nutritional status, immune status, and genetic susceptibility — that influence disease occurrence.
Incorrect. The agent refers to the causative factor (biological, chemical, physical, or nutritional) that must be present for disease to occur. Susceptibility characteristics belong to the host.
Incorrect. The environment includes all external factors (physical, biological, socio-economic) that surround the host. Intrinsic individual characteristics belong to the host component.
Incorrect. A vector is an organism (often an arthropod) that transmits an agent to the host — it is not a component of the epidemiological triad itself, though it operates within the environment.

overallFeedback.feedback: The epidemiological triad has three components: agent (causative factor), host (intrinsic characteristics of the individual), and environment (external surroundings). Age, sex, immunity, and genetic susceptibility all belong to the host.
Good. Host factors determine individual susceptibility and modify the probability of disease given agent-environment interaction.
